summary: The Jinja `range()` function now always returns a range object, which cannot be returned from a template unless converted to a returnable type such as a list.
questions: Why does range() behave differently in ansible-core 2.19?
Can I return range() directly from a template?

answer_card.title: range() always returns a range object
answer_card.answer_md: Previously the result of Jinja's `range()` depended on context and whether native mode was on. To support very large ranges in filter chains, it now **always returns a range object**, which can't be returned from a template unless you convert it (for example with `| list`).
